 Order

W.P.No.200101/2024 is filed to quash the order dated 29.11.2023 passed by the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal in Rev.Appeal No.192/2022 as well as the order dated 31.03.2022 passed by the respondent No.1 in Rev/Con/CR-460/2019-20.

The petitioner has also sought for a writ in the nature of mandamus to direct the respondent No.1 to consider the online application dated 05.08.2019 for conversion of the land to non- agricultural purposes.

The petitioner claims to have purchased an extent of 1 acre 24 guntas of land in Sy.No.4/4 of Naubad Village, Bidar District from its erstwhile owner Sri. Tukaram, S/o Manik in terms of the sale deed dated 28.10.2016.

Consequent to the sale, revenue proceedings were initiated to enter the name of the petitioner in MR No.H14/2016-17 and the name of the petitioner was entered in the revenue records for the year 2019-20 and onwards.
The petitioner filed an application for conversion of the aforesaid land for non-agricultural purposes on 08.05.2019.
This application was rejected in terms of an endorsement dated 05.08.2019 on the ground that the Tahsildar had reported that the application for conversion be rejected.

The petitioner challenged this endorsement Mohammed Bashrat Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17517439/
3 before the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal, Bengaluru, in Appeal No.170/2020.

entities.text: Mohammed Bashrat Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Appellate Tribunal in terms of its order dated 27.01.2021 allowed the appeal and set aside the endorsement issued by the Deputy Commissioner and directed reconsideration of the request of the petitioner for conversion of the land.

On such remand, the Deputy Commissioner again held proceedings and found that the land in Sy.No.4/4 of Naubad village was acquired by the State Government for the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3338 purposes of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (henceforth referred to as 'KIADB').
He therefore, held that the petitioner was not the owner of the land and therefore, was not entitled for conversion of the land for non-agricultural purposes.
The petitioner challenged the said order before the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal, Bengaluru, in Rev.Appeal No.192/2022.

The Appellate Tribunal in terms of its order dated 29.11.2023 held that once a land was acquired, the Junior Engineer attached to the office of the KIADB had no business to issue a declaration that the land was mistakenly acquired.
It therefore, held that the appeal filed by the petitioner before it was without any merit and consequently, dismissed it in terms of the order dated 29.11.2023.

The petitioner is therefore, before this Court challenging the order passed by the Appellate Tribunal as well as the order rejecting the application filed by him before the Deputy Commissioner for conversion of his land for non-agricultural purposes.

3. W.P.No.225827/2020 is filed challenging an order 31.03.2020 passed by the respondent No.2 in Case No.BHU/PA/CR-460/2019-20 and for a writ in the nature of Mandamus to direct the respondents to restore the revenue NC: 2024:KHC-K:3338 entries in respect of the land bearing Sy.No.4/4, measuring 1 acre 24 guntas situate at Naubad village, Bidar District in the name of the petitioner.
4. The Deputy Commissioner following the order passed by the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal,

initiated suo moto proceedings and passed an order dated 31.3.2020 to enter the name of the KIADB in Column Nos.9 and 12(2) of the RTC and suspended the Village Accountant and the Revenue Inspector for bringing about the revenue records in respect of the Sy.No.4/4 in the name of the petitioner by deleting the name of KIADB in RTC for the year 1994 till 1998-99.
He also suspended the village accountant and the revenue inspector for entering the name of the petitioner pursuant to MR No.H14/16- 17 dated 21.12.2016.

He also directed initiation of action against one Sri. Shashikanth Patil, who had formed sites in Sy.Nos.4/4, 11 and 12/1 of Naubad village, by prosecuting him for the offences punishable under Section 192-A of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

He also directed the Sub- Registrar, Bidar not to register any documents relating to any portion of the property in Sy.Nos.4/4, 11 and 12/1 of Naubad village and directed the Commissioner,
City Municipal Council, NC: 2024:KHC-K:3338 Bidar to forthwith take steps for cancellation of khatas registered in respect of any portion of the land in Sy.Nos.4/4, 11 and 12/1 and directed the Development Officer of KIADB to take over possession of the land bearing Sy.Nos.4/4, 11 and 12/1.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioner in W.P.No.200101/2024 contended that an Engineer attached to the office of the KIADB had issued an endorsement dated 09.05.2000 stating therein that the land bearing Sy.No.4/4 was mistakenly acquired and that the compensation was not paid to the owners of the land.
He therefore, contends that there was no impediment for the respondents to convert the land in question.

He further contends that the KIADB has not taken any action against the concerned Engineer and hence, the impugned order passed by the Deputy Commissioner Mohammed Bashrat Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17517439/
4 refusing to convert the land for non-agricultural purposes deserves to be interfered with.

entities.text: Deputy Commissioner Mohammed Bashrat Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further contends that the name of the petitioner is continuously entered in the revenue records and several other revenue and survey proceedings are initiated at his behest, which indicates that the land was not acquired.

He therefore, contends that the impugned orders passed by the NC:
2024:KHC-K:3338 Deputy Commissioner as well as the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal be interfered with.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioner in W.P.No.225827/2020 contends that the order passed by the Deputy Commissioner to restore the name of the KIADB in respect of the land in Sy.No.4/4 and to cancel all the khatas in respect of portion of the property bearing Sy.No.4/4 in the records of the City Municipal Council, Bidar, was without notice to him and without hearing him.

He therefore,
contends that the impugned order passed by the Deputy Commissioner has to be set aside only on the sole ground of non-compliance of principles of natural justice.
7.

Per contra, learned counsel for the KIADB/Board submits that the land bearing Sy.No.4/4 of Naubad village, Bidar District, measuring 1 acre 24 guntas was proposed to be acquired under Section 28(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.

He submits that a final notification under Section 28(3) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act was issued on 06.12.1983 and was published in the Official Gazette, which indicated that 1 acre 24 guntas in NC:
2024:KHC-K:3338 Sy.No.4/4 of Naubad village was acquired.

He also contended that the compensation of Rs.50,500/- was received by the erstwhile owners of the land bearing Sy.Nos.4/4 and 4/5 and the possession of the land was taken over by the Land Acquisition Officer and handed over to the KIADB.
He submits that the revenue entries were brought about in Column No.11 of the RTC, which indicated the name of the KIADB.

He therefore, contends that the petitioner had purchased a property that was duly acquired by the State Government for the purposes of KIADB and therefore, the petitioner was not the owner entitled to convert the land for non-agricultural purposes.
He submits that the endorsement issued by the Junior Engineer of the Board is inconsequential in the face of the notification.

He further contends that since the land is acquired by the State Government for the purpose of the Board, there is no error committed by the Deputy Commissioner in directing the restoration of the name of the KIADB and also in passing further orders to ensure that the property is duly protected.

8. Learned High Court Government Pleader on the other hand submitted that pursuant to an order passed by this - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3338 Court to identify the limits of the land acquired by the State Government for the purpose of Board, a survey was conducted in the presence of the petitioner as well as the respondent - Board.

It showed that the entire extent of land in Sy.No.4/4 was acquired and hence,
the order passed by the Deputy Commissioner refusing to convert the land in question for non- agricultural purposes does not warrant any interference.

entities.text: Mohammed Bashrat Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner in both the petitions and learned counsel for the Board as well as the learned High Court Government Pleader.
I have also perused the records produced before the Court.
10. The land in question is Sy.No.4/4 of Naubad village, Bidar District, measuring 1 acre 24 guntas.

A perusal of the notification produced by the learned counsel for the Board establishes that the entire extent of 1 acre 24 guntas of land in Sy.No.4/4 was notified in the names of the predecessors of the vendors of the petitioner.

The documents produced by the learned counsel for the Board also establish that the possession of the land was taken over by the officers of the State - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3338 Government and handed over to the board for further action.

Therefore, the endorsement issued by a Junior Engineer attached to the Board that the land was mistakenly acquired is apparently fraudulent and concocted for the purpose of creating records in favour of the petitioner.

In the face of the acquisition of the land, it stood vested in the KIADB and consequent sale deed executed in favour of the petitioner and the revenue records following such sale, were all inconsequential and did not confer any right, title or interest in favour of the petitioner.

Therefore,
the petitioner was not entitled to seek for conversion of the land for non-agricultural purposes.
The reasoning of the Deputy Commissioner in refusing to grant conversion of the land in question, is just and proper and does not call for interference.

11. In so far as further action taken by the Deputy Commissioner to secure the interest of the Board,
this Court does not find any reason to hear the petitioner as the petitioner was in no way concerned with the land in question and therefore, he was not entitled to be heard before passing the impugned order to safeguard the interest of the Board by directing the Sub-Registrar not to entertain any document for - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3338 registration and also in directing Commissioner of the Municipal Council to cancel all the khatha made out in respect of the land in Sy.No.4/4 and other ancillary directions.

There is no error committed by the official respondents in not acceding to the request of the petitioner for conversion of the land and also in taking steps to protect the interest of the Board in respect of the land bearing Sy.Nos.4/4, 11 and 12/1 of Naubad village, Bidar District warranting interference by this Court in these writ petitions.
12. Hence, these writ petitions lack merit and are dismissed.
